title: Tamsin and the Signal
premise: Paloma Vasquez, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists still in cryosleep, is the last regular courier between two human worlds that severed contact generations ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, he discovers the sleeping colonists are not one crew but two rival factions — and the ship's failing reactor will only allow half of them to wake. As Paloma races to decode the signal's true source, he uncovers that the 'extinct' language belongs to a third ship, long lost, whose survivors have been waiting in the dark. In the end, Paloma must choose which half wakes — and instead finds a way to merge the factions' cryo-systems with the lost ship's, waking everyone slowly across decades, building the found family he never had.
about_author: A. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things alive in unforgiving places.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He pilots his courier vessel between Colony Meridian and the silent world Halcyon, tending seedlings en route. Establishes his isolation, his ritual care for plants meant for strangers, and the ache of routes where no one answers anymore. Beat: lonely competence.

chapters.title: Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Paloma tends the orbital greenhouse above Meridian, recording messages for colonists who may never wake. A supervisor hints budget cuts may end the courier run entirely. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Static in an Old Tongue
chapters.summary: During a supply stop, Paloma's receiver catches a repeating distress signal — in Vessic, a language extinct since the Sundering. He verifies it three times before believing it. Beat: wonder cracking through routine.

chapters.title: Nobody Speaks It Anymore
chapters.summary: Paloma seeks out archivist Ione Sable, the only person on Meridian who studies dead languages. She confirms the signal is genuine Vessic — and predates known colony launches. Beat: the mystery deepens; first alliance.

chapters.title: Permission Denied
chapters.summary: Meridian's council forbids investigation: contact with pre-Sundering signals violates treaty law. Paloma decides to go anyway, taking Ione as translator. Beat: defiance born of duty.

chapters.title: Departure Without Blessing
chapters.summary: Paloma loads the greenhouse seeds aboard as ballast and slips out past the patrol grid. Ione decodes the signal's origin coordinates: a region of space marked only as 'the Quiet.' Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Quiet
chapters.summary: En route, they find debris fields from ships history forgot. Ione translates fragments: the distress call isn't asking for rescue — it's asking to be remembered. Beat: scale of loss sinks in.

chapters.title: Halcyon Answers
chapters.summary: Halcyon, the silent world, suddenly transmits — warning them away in modern Standard. Someone there is alive, watching, and afraid. Beat: the silence was chosen.

chapters.title: Docking at Dusk
chapters.summary: Against warnings, Paloma lands. He meets Wren Okafor, Halcyon's reluctant administrator, who reveals Halcyon shelters descendants of the Vessic-speaking ship's crew. Beat: first contact with the 'lost.'

chapters.title: Children of the Lost Ship
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Halcyon community kept Vessic alive in secret for two centuries, believing Meridian abandoned them. The distress signal was their desperate gamble. Beat: grief and resentment on both sides.

chapters.title: What the Signal Said
chapters.summary: Ione finishes translating: the signal warns that the sleeper ship Perpetua — carrying both colonies' frozen ancestors — has a failing reactor and twelve months of power left. Half its sleepers will die. Beat: stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Two Halves of One Manifest
chapters.summary: Perpetua's manifest splits into two factions: Meridian's founders and Halcyon's. The reactor can wake one group fully or both partially. Old factional hatred resurfaces instantly. Beat: the central dilemma crystallizes.

chapters.title: Councils and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Joint session between Meridian's remote council and Halcyon's elders collapses into recrimination over the Sundering. Paloma watches the families of the dead argue over the dying. Beat: frustration, moral weight.

chapters.title: The Reactor Room
chapters.summary: Paloma and Wren fly to Perpetua itself. Inside, rows upon rows of sleepers — thousands of faces, including children. Paloma recognizes the garden design etched on the walls: his own greenhouse's blueprint. Beat: awe and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Blueprints of Belonging
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through recovered logs: Perpetua's original engineer designed the gardens so both factions would share one living space upon waking. The plan died with her. Beat: hope found in the past.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone drains power reserves overnight. Evidence points to a Halcyon hardliner who wants Meridian's sleepers written off. Wren arrests her own cousin. Beat: trust fractures within the found family.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The cousin claims Meridian sabotaged Halcyon first, two centuries ago — the severance wasn't mutual abandonment but an attack. Beat: the story both sides believed begins to unravel.

chapters.title: Reading the Black Box
chapters.summary: Ione and Paloma recover Perpetua's flight recorder. The truth: a third party, the Consortium, engineered the severance to claim Perpetua's route and resources. Both colonies were played. Beat: revelation reframes everything.

chapters.title: The Consortium Still Exists
chapters.summary: A Consortium salvage fleet is inbound to strip Perpetua — the reactor failure may be their doing. Twelve months becomes four. Beat: external threat compresses the clock.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Meridian's council, shamed by the black box evidence, sends technical aid — and its own hardliners. Paloma mediates between delegations who share tools but not trust. Beat: fragile coalition-building.

chapters.title: Teaching Each Other Tongues
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Ione teaches Meridian engineers Vessic; Halcyon youth learn Meridian horticulture. Paloma watches two peoples become, tentatively, a crew. Beat: warmth, belonging taking root.

chapters.title: The Garden Experiment
chapters.summary: Paloma proposes merging Perpetua's cryo-systems with the greenhouse biosphere — using the gardens' thermal mass to slow decay and wake sleepers gradually. The engineers say it might work. Beat: the plan is born.

chapters.title: First Graft
chapters.summary: They connect the first biothermal loop. One sleeper's vitals stabilize beyond projections. Paloma names the loop after the lost engineer, Ada Reyes. Beat: cautious triumph.

chapters.title: Consortium Vanguard
chapters.summary: A Consortium scout ship arrives demanding Perpetua under a two-century-old salvage claim. Paloma refuses; the scout withdraws, promising the fleet. Beat: dread returns.

chapters.title: Evacuation Debate
chapters.summary: Some argue waking everyone now, even damaged, beats losing all to the Consortium. Others insist the graft method needs time. Paloma is asked to decide as neutral party. Beat: the choice he dreaded arrives early.

chapters.title: Paloma's Choice
chapters.summary: Paloma refuses to choose halves: he commits to finishing the full graft network in ninety days, staking everything — including his own life support allocation — on it. Beat: sacrifice declared.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Montage-style chapter: shifts around the clock, failures and fixes, Ione collapsing from exhaustion, Wren holding the factions together. Day 61: the network is 70% complete. Beat: grinding perseverance.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Airlock
chapters.summary: A Meridian hardliner opens Perpetua's hull section to force emergency waking — which would kill the graft network. Wren takes the breach himself to seal it. Beat: devastating cost.

chapters.title: Wren's Hands
chapters.summary: Wren survives, radiation-sickened, in medical stasis beside the very sleepers he saved. Paloma keeps vigil, finally understanding family is who you stay up nights for. Beat: grief transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: The Consortium fleet drops out of transit with boarding intentions. The graft is 90% complete. Paloma broadcasts Perpetua's manifest to every human channel: these are citizens, not salvage. Beat: climax approaches.

chapters.title: Signal to All Worlds
chapters.summary: Ione's masterstroke: rebroadcasting the original Vessic distress call plus the black box evidence system-wide. Other colonies respond — observers, journalists, warships of their own. Beat: the tide turns publicly.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: Consortium marines board anyway. Paloma, engineers, and Halcyon defenders hold the reactor ring while the final graft loops close. Hand-to-hand in the dark among sleeping ancestors. Beat: physical climax.

chapters.title: Closing the Last Loop
chapters.summary: With minutes left, Paloma manually seals the final biothermal junction inside a flooding compartment, mirroring Ada Reyes' original sacrifice. The network completes. Every sleeper stabilizes. Beat: climax resolved at personal cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: The Consortium withdraws under public scrutiny. Paloma, injured but alive, walks the merged garden as systems hum. The first scheduled wakings begin — ten people per month, mixed from both factions. Beat: exhale.

chapters.title: First Waking
chapters.summary: Ada Reyes' descendant — a young woman carrying the family name — wakes to find strangers of both worlds holding vigil, speaking a blend of two tongues. She asks who tended the garden. Beat: emotional payoff.

chapters.title: Telling the Story
chapters.summary: Paloma records the message he always promised the unborn: the whole truth of the Sundering, the sabotage, the choice refused. Ione archives it in both languages. Beat: reckoning and honesty.

chapters.title: Reconciliation Is Work
chapters.summary: Time-skip: joint governance forms on Perpetua. Hardliners on both sides grumble; children raised together don't care. Wren, recovering, is elected to lead the waking program. Beat: earned, imperfect peace.

chapters.title: The Route Reopened
chapters.summary: Paloma flies the Meridian–Halcyon route again — now busy with traffic, messages, trade. The silence between worlds is broken for good. He carries seedlings and letters alike. Beat: restoration.

chapters.title: Family, Found
chapters.summary: Final gathering aboard Perpetua: Paloma, Ione, Wren, the newly woken, the garden in bloom. Paloma realizes the garden was never for strangers — it was waiting for him too. Beat: belonging achieved.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Signal
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Paloma's POV years later. A child named Tamsin, born aboard Perpetua to parents from both worlds, asks about the old distress signal. Paloma teaches her Vessic's word for home. The signal, once a cry, is now a lullaby. Beat: legacy and peace.
